Dialogue: I found the school at the address Annie had given me.
The music room was on one side of the school building. The wall outside was covered with music posters, and there was a group photo of the student band.
This should be it.
I stopped in front of the music room and knocked.
Come in.
I pushed the door open and saw a middle-aged woman sitting inside, sorting sheet music. A violin lay beside her. It looked like she’d just finished practicing.
Hello. Are you Maria, the music teacher?
Yes. And you are?
I'm here to ask about Elena.
The teacher’s hands paused.
Elena? You know her?
Sort of. I’m arranging her funeral, and I’d like to get in touch with some people who knew her.
Her funeral?
She seemed a little taken aback.
She's...
Yes. She passed away.
The teacher was silent for a while.
I never expected this. I hardly heard from her after she left school.
Did you teach her?
Yeah. She used to go to my music class with a girl named Annie.
Annie has promised to come to the funeral.
Annie? Is she still around here?
I heard that she now occasionally plays in bars and on the streets.
I see. The kid used to love music.
She looked at the violin on the table.
Annie was more lively, Elena was much more quiet.
They used to practice together?
Sometimes. But they seem to like talking more than practice.
What do they talk about?
The teacher laughed.
There's everything. There's something going on in school, and there's something going on. The kids at that age, they always think it's possible.
What was Elena like before?
She's a special kid. She's always sitting at the end of class, not talking to people.
She doesn't like music lessons?
Not really. She's just a little out of her league.
The teacher's done the table.
But then something happened that gave me a different impression of her.
What's going on?
You can look at photos and posters outside. They should remind you of something.
All right.
I saw a few posters on the wall that were left behind by the previous school music event.
These posters seem to have been in place for some years.
Yeah, it's all from the old school.
Elena, have you ever been to these events before?
Have participated once.
Did she sign up?
No. There was a concert at the school where students were asked to participate as much as possible. She was reluctant to perform in person, but eventually she did.
How's she playing?
I'm surprised.
Why?
She performed the harmonica at the time. She never showed it in class, but she did well when she actually stood on the stage.
She used to play the harmonica?
I think she likes blowing.
Did you encourage her to continue?
Of course. I think she has a gift for it, and I want her to try something she likes more.
Does she want to?
She did not refuse, except that it was as if more and more things had happened in her home and that she did not have much time.
The teacher looked at the poster.
Sometimes I think a child's interest doesn't have to be a profession. It's good to have something that he wants to do.
I think so, too.
I've had a moment myself to say that.
I don't know why, I seem to agree with that very naturally.
I went to another picture.
The picture is of a group of students standing together, with guitars, music notes and several people standing next to musical instruments.
Is this a former student band?
Yeah. There was a lot of music at school.
Elena and Annie are in there?
Well, they've all been to some events.
I looked closely at the pictures.
They're standing together.
Annie was more outward, often pulling Elena into the event.
Elena doesn't look like much of a photographer.
Ha ha, you're right. Every time she takes a picture she likes to hide behind, Annie likes to stand in the front.
It seems that their personalities are not the same.
Yeah, but two of them kind of got along.
Why didn't they keep in touch?
I don't know. After graduation, the students have their own lives, and some of the relationships have faded.
Do you want to see them again if you have a chance?
Of course. Especially Elena.
She looked at the picture and sneezed.
I always felt there was a lot of things I couldn't say to her.
Would you like to come to her funeral?
The teacher turned around and looked at me.
Of course.
Thank you.
You don't have to thank me. Thank you for doing this for her.
I'm back in class.
Maria started working on the score, and there was a violin on the table.
Teacher, do you practice here?
Yeah. I practice sometimes when there's nothing going on at school.
Have you played the violin long?
It's been years. I've been learning the piano for years.
Will it still be hard?
The teacher laughed.
Yeah. But there are some things that become habit when they're done.
I'm looking for a score from the teacher.
Is this for your usual practice?
Yeah, I've been practicing a song lately.
Looks complicated.
It's okay. It's not about whether you can pull it out, it's about whether you can really express it.
Sounds pretty hard.
Of course it's hard.
She smiled.
But Elena used to like to listen to others. Although she wasn't particularly obsessed with some kind of instrument, she still had her own feelings for music.
Did she discuss this with you before?
Occasionally. Sometimes she asks me, "Why does it feel different when different people play the same song?"
What did you say to her?
I told her because everyone has their own experience and ideas. Music is just one way to express these things.
Does she understand?
I think she understands a little bit.
I looked at that violin again.
Teacher, the piano looks well maintained.
Well, I usually check it regularly.
Did you just practice this piano?
Yeah. You want to hear it?
May I?
Sure.
Maria picked up the violin, slightly repositioned the bow, and then played a little tune.
The music was ringing in the classroom.
I'm not talking, just listening quietly.
What do you think?
That's nice.
Have you ever learned music before?
I don't remember.
Don't you remember?
Maybe a little. I just can't remember now.
The teacher didn't keep asking.
Elena used to do the same thing. Sometimes she listens to a piece of music and suddenly quiets, like what she thinks.
Does she like that feeling?
I think so.
Did she come back later?
I came back once in a while, but it was a long time ago.
Do you remember what she said?
She didn't say anything special. She just asked me if people could become another person when they left their original lives.
I'm stunned.
What did you say?
I told her, of course. It's just that wherever you go, you can't completely forget who you were.
What did she say?
She smiled and said she knew.
The teacher put the violin back on the table.
At the time, I thought she might have figured out the way to go.
I look back at Maria.
Teacher, did you just say Elena was in a bad family condition?
Yeah.
Can you talk to me?
The teacher was silent.
Her mother died very early and was raised by her father.
How did she get along with her father?
I don't know much about it. She rarely talks about her family.
So how do you know about her home?
One time she was not feeling well at school and I contacted her father to learn something.
What happened to her father?
Her father's eyesight is worse than it is, and he can no longer work long hours.
So your family's in a bad financial situation?
Elena later had to work after school, subsidized the family.
She was still in school, wasn't she?
Well, she's been working hard, but there's something she doesn't have to take on at her age.
Has she ever complained to you?
Very rarely. She always says she's fine and doesn't want anyone to worry about her.
Why didn't she ask for help?
Maybe he didn't want to cause any trouble.
I'm down, I'm not talking.
But I can't understand much more. After all, it's her family, and I can't really do much more.
Do you think she's happy?
The teacher didn't answer immediately.
I don't know.
She looked out the window.
But I hope that she will have the opportunity to live her life as she thinks.
She should hope so too.
The teacher looked at me.
You seem to care about her.
Maybe it's because I don't think a person should just leave silently.
Yeah.
I've contacted her old friend, and now I've found you. If I can, I'd like to have more people who know her at the funeral.
I'll go.
Thank you.
You're welcome. It's just...
What's wrong?
If you see her father, can you say hello to him for me?
You know him?
I've been in touch a few times before, but I haven't seen you since.
All right.
And, about Elena, if you know anything later, you can tell me.
Okay.
I said goodbye to Maria and left the music class.
When I walked out of the school building, I looked back.
Through the window, I can also see that the teacher is working on the violin.
I don't know why, just when I heard the music, I had a feeling of familiarity that I couldn't say.
But I didn't think much.
At least now, another person would like to come to Elena's funeral.
